origins.section: The Solver Is an Argument to solve, Never Part of the Model
CP-SAT Needs Integers, and Rounds a Continuous Model Without Warning
Each Solver Accepts Only the Model Types It Can Solve, and Says So Before Solving

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-switch: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-switch: "The solver went in as a value ... and nothing else in the program changed"; "the model builder knows nothing of solvers".
recorded.prompt:q-cpsat: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-cpsat: "CP-SAT stopped at a = 8, a whole number, and still said OPTIMAL ... it is just not the optimum of the model you wrote"; HiGHS gave the true optimum.
recorded.prompt:q-scip-lp: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-scip-lp: "SCIP solves the LP and returns no duals at all"; GSCIP showed "OPTIMAL 23,669.5 no duals". This page does not name ValueError, but c is the only option consistent with "no duals".
